_meta.why: NVIDIA publishes SASS mnemonics but not postfix semantics. This table fills that gap. Every entry carries a `source` so a tooltip can say how well grounded it is instead of presenting all of it as fact.
_meta.lookup: An opcode-specific entry wins over a group entry, which wins over `generic`. Group membership is by exact opcode name; the `U`-prefixed uniform-datapath twin of an opcode (UIADD3 for IADD3) is resolved automatically by the extension.

sources.ptx: Semantics documented in the PTX ISA for the corresponding PTX instruction, which SASS mirrors closely.
sources.slides: Stated in the GPGPU Arch 07 - NVIDIA Ampere deep dive lecture notes.
sources.community: Established by published reverse-engineering, chiefly arXiv:1903.07486 (Dissecting the NVidia Turing T4 GPU) and the Maxwell-era assembler work.
sources.corpus: Read off observed disassembly; the reading is consistent with every occurrence seen but is not independently confirmed.

RN.desc: Round to nearest, ties to even. The IEEE-754 default; usually implicit and only spelled out when it needs to override something.

RZ.desc: Round toward zero (truncate). As a *postfix* this is a rounding mode - not to be confused with the `RZ` zero register in an operand slot.

FTZ.desc: Flush denormals to zero. Subnormal inputs and results are replaced by a same-signed zero. Faster, and not IEEE-754 conformant - this is what `-ftz=true` and most graphics compilers produce by default.

DNZ.desc: Denormals are zero on *input* only; the result may still be subnormal.

SAT.desc: Saturate the result to [0.0, 1.0]. NaN becomes 0.0.

RELU.desc: Clamp the result at zero from below (max(0, x)), leaving NaN as NaN. Fused activation, cheaper than a separate FMNMX.

XORSIGN.desc: The result takes the XOR of the operand sign bits.

NAN.desc: Propagate NaN rather than returning the non-NaN operand.

ABS.desc: Take the absolute value of the operand before use.

U32.desc: Operand type: unsigned 32-bit. On a comparison this selects the unsigned ordering; SASS defaults to signed, so `.U32` is the one that gets printed.

F64.desc: Operand type: IEEE double precision (a register pair).

BF16.desc: Operand type: bfloat16 - FP32's 8-bit exponent with a 7-bit mantissa. Same range as FP32, far less precision.

TF32.desc: Operand type: TensorFloat-32 - FP32 exponent range truncated to a 10-bit mantissa. A tensor-core input format, not a storage format.

E4M3.desc: Operand type: FP8 with a 4-bit exponent and 3-bit mantissa (more precision, less range).

E5M2.desc: Operand type: FP8 with a 5-bit exponent and 2-bit mantissa (more range, less precision).

H2.desc: Packed pair of halves in one 32-bit register; the operation runs on both lanes at once.

LT.desc: Compare: less than. False if either operand is NaN.

LE.desc: Compare: less than or equal. False if either operand is NaN.

EQ.desc: Compare: equal. False if either operand is NaN.

NE.desc: Compare: not equal. False if either operand is NaN.

GE.desc: Compare: greater than or equal. False if either operand is NaN.

GT.desc: Compare: greater than. False if either operand is NaN.

LTU.desc: Compare: less than **or unordered** - also true when either operand is NaN.

LEU.desc: Compare: less-or-equal **or unordered** - also true when either operand is NaN.

EQU.desc: Compare: equal **or unordered** - also true when either operand is NaN.

NEU.desc: Compare: not-equal **or unordered** - also true when either operand is NaN.

GEU.desc: Compare: greater-or-equal **or unordered**. The trailing `U` folds NaN into the *true* side, so a NaN takes the branch IEEE-754 would have sent the other way. This is how a compiler inverts `a < b` without introducing a NaN discrepancy of its own.

GTU.desc: Compare: greater-than **or unordered** - also true when either operand is NaN.

NUM.desc: Compare: ordered - true when neither operand is NaN.

AND.desc: Combine the comparison result with the incoming predicate operand using AND. The trailing `PT` in the operand list is the identity for it, which is why unconditioned compares end in `, PT`.

OR.desc: Combine the comparison result with the incoming predicate operand using OR.

XOR.desc: Combine the comparison result with the incoming predicate operand using XOR.

64.desc: 64-bit access width - two consecutive registers, and the base register must be even-aligned.

128.desc: 128-bit access width - four consecutive registers, aligned to a multiple of four. The widest single memory transaction, and what the compiler reaches for to cut instruction count on contiguous data.

E.desc: Extended address: the address operand is a 64-bit register pair rather than a 32-bit offset.

STRONG.desc: Strongly-ordered access - participates in the memory model's ordering at the given scope. Pairs with a scope postfix such as `.SM` or `.GPU`.

WEAK.desc: Weakly-ordered access - no ordering guarantee beyond the same thread.

CONSTANT.desc: Non-coherent read-only path (the `__ldg` / texture cache route). Valid only when nothing writes the location for the lifetime of the kernel.

MMIO.desc: Memory-mapped I/O access; not cached, not reordered.

PRIVATE.desc: Thread-private access - the compiler knows no other thread can observe it.

CTA.desc: Scope: the thread block. Ordering is guaranteed only among threads of the same CTA.

SM.desc: Scope: the SM. Broader than `.CTA`, narrower than `.GPU` - the usual choice for shared-memory-backed traffic.

GPU.desc: Scope: the whole device. Ordering is guaranteed across all CTAs on the GPU.

SYS.desc: Scope: the system, including the host and peer devices. The most expensive scope.

EF.desc: Cache hint: evict first. Mark the line as the next candidate for eviction - for streaming data you will not revisit.

EL.desc: Cache hint: evict last. Keep the line as long as possible - for data you will revisit.

LU.desc: Cache hint: last use. This read is the final one, so the line may be dropped immediately afterwards.

EU.desc: Cache hint: evict unchanged - do not disturb the line's existing eviction priority.

NA.desc: Cache hint: no allocate. Do not bring the line into the cache at all.

ZD.desc: Zero-detect: additionally write a predicate saying whether the loaded value was zero.

X.desc: Extended precision: consume a carry/borrow predicate produced by a previous instruction, so a pair of 32-bit ops forms one 64-bit op.

HI.desc: Take the high half of the double-width result.

WIDE.desc: Produce the full double-width result into a register pair (32x32 -> 64).

CC.desc: Also write the condition code / carry-out.

reuse.desc: Operand reuse cache hit. The operand-collector already holds this value from the previous instruction, so re-reading it costs no register-file bandwidth. Emitted by the compiler as a scheduling hint - it changes power and issue pressure, never the result.

NZ.desc: Test the result for non-zero and write it to the predicate destination.

Z.desc: Test the result for zero and write it to the predicate destination.

FLOOR.desc: Convert by rounding toward minus infinity.

CEIL.desc: Convert by rounding toward plus infinity.

NTZ.desc: Convert by rounding to nearest, ties toward zero.

DESC.desc: Descriptor-based addressing: the access goes through a memory descriptor held in a uniform register, spelled `desc[UR4]`. This is how bindless/bindful resource access reaches global memory in graphics and in newer compute ABIs.

U.desc: Uniform: the operation is known to be warp-invariant and runs on the uniform datapath.

mufu.desc: Multi-function unit operation select. One SFU instruction, many transcendentals - the postfix picks which.

RCP.desc: Reciprocal, 1/x. Fast approximate; a full-precision divide is this plus Newton-Raphson refinement steps.

RSQ.desc: Reciprocal square root, 1/sqrt(x). The natural primitive for `normalize()` - which is why normalize compiles to a dot product, MUFU.RSQ, and two multiplies rather than a divide.

SIN.desc: Sine. The argument is pre-scaled by 1/2pi, which is where the 0.15915493667125701904 multiply just before it comes from.

COS.desc: Cosine, on the same 1/2pi-scaled argument as `.SIN`.

TANH.desc: Hyperbolic tangent. Added for activation functions.

RCP64H.desc: Reciprocal seed from the high 32 bits of an FP64 value - the first step of a double-precision divide.

RSQ64H.desc: Reciprocal-square-root seed from the high 32 bits of an FP64 value.

imad.desc: Integer multiply-add, and the compiler idioms built on it.

MOV.desc: Move idiom: `IMAD.MOV.U32 Rd, RZ, RZ, src` computes 0*0 + src, i.e. a plain move. The compiler emits it instead of `MOV` to spread work across pipelines - on Ampere the FMA-heavy datapath can retire it while the ALU datapath is busy, so it is a scheduling choice, not arithmetic.

IADD.desc: Add idiom: multiply by one to perform an addition on the multiply pipeline, again for issue-slot balance.

SHL.desc: Shift-left idiom: multiply by a power of two.

WIDE.desc: Full 32x32 -> 64 product into a register pair. Common in address arithmetic, where a 32-bit index has to reach a 64-bit pointer.

HI.desc: Keep only the high 32 bits of the 64-bit product.

X.desc: Consume a carry-in predicate, extending the add half to a wider precision.

LUT.desc: The trailing 8-bit immediate is a truth table over the three inputs, not a value. Bit *i* of the immediate gives the output for the input combination whose binary digits are *i*: `0xc0` = a AND b, `0xfc` = a OR b, `0x3c` = a XOR b, `0xf0` = a. One instruction covers every 3-input boolean function.

PAND.desc: AND the result with the incoming predicate before writing.

HI.desc: Take the high word of the funnel-shift result. A funnel shift concatenates two registers and shifts the 64-bit pair; `.HI` selects which half is kept.

W.desc: Wrap the shift amount modulo the operand width instead of clamping.

CLAMP.desc: Clamp a shift amount larger than the operand width to the width, yielding 0 or the sign fill.

WRAP.desc: Wrap a shift amount larger than the operand width modulo the width.

EX.desc: Extended compare: fold in the predicate from the low half so that two 32-bit compares implement one 64-bit compare.

BF.desc: Write the boolean result as a float (0.0 or 1.0) into a general register rather than to a predicate. This is what turns a branchless `a < b` into a value you can multiply by.

NAN.desc: Compare: unordered - true when either input is NaN.

AND.desc: Combine the comparison result with the incoming predicate operand using AND. The trailing `PT` is the identity, which is why unconditioned compares end in `, PT`.

branch.desc: Branches, calls, and the convergence-barrier instructions that bracket divergent regions.

U.desc: Uniform branch: the whole warp is known to agree, so no divergence stack work is needed.

DIV.desc: Divergent branch: lanes may disagree and the hardware must split the warp.

CONV.desc: Convergent branch: the warp is expected to reconverge at the target.

REL.desc: Target is relative to the program counter.

NOINC.desc: Do not push a return address - a tail call, or a call whose return is handled by other means.

INC.desc: Push a return address onto the call stack.

NODEC.desc: Return without popping the call stack.

ALL.desc: Wait for every lane in the mask before proceeding.

EXCLUSIVE.desc: Only the lanes in the mask participate; the rest continue.

CLEAR.desc: Clear the source convergence-barrier state after moving it.

E.desc: Extended address: a 64-bit register pair holds the address. Standard for global memory on a 64-bit ABI.

SM.desc: Scope: the SM. In `STG.E.STRONG.SM` the access is ordered with respect to other threads on the same SM but not device-wide.

BYPASS.desc: Bypass L1 and go straight to L2 - for the asynchronous copy path, where staging through L1 would be wasted work.

ACCESS.desc: Take the normal cached path rather than bypassing.

LTC128B.desc: 128-byte L2 cache-line granularity hint for the access.

SYS.desc: Scope: system-wide, covering the host and peer devices.

atomic.desc: The read-modify-write operation an atomic performs.

INC.desc: Atomic increment with wraparound at a supplied limit.

DEC.desc: Atomic decrement with wraparound at a supplied limit.

EXCH.desc: Atomic exchange - swap in the new value and return the old one.

SAFEADD.desc: Atomic add that saturates rather than wrapping on overflow.

ldsm.desc: Warp-level matrix loads from shared memory.

M88.desc: Use an 8 by 8 matrix fragment layout.

4.desc: Load four matrix fragments into four consecutive, naturally aligned destination registers.

SX32.desc: Sign-extend the 32-bit address contribution before combining it.

SC.desc: Sequentially consistent ordering at the selected scope.

UP.desc: Shuffle from a lower lane index.

DOWN.desc: Shuffle from a higher lane index.

BFLY.desc: Butterfly shuffle - exchange with the lane whose index differs by the given XOR mask. The reduction-tree primitive.

ALL.desc: True when the predicate holds in every active lane.

ANY.desc: True when the predicate holds in at least one active lane.

EQ.desc: True when every active lane agrees on the predicate.

BALLOT.desc: Return the predicate of every lane as a 32-bit mask.

SYNC.desc: Arrive at the barrier and wait for the other participants.

ARV.desc: Arrive at the barrier without waiting.

RED.desc: Barrier with reduction - combine a per-thread value while synchronising.

POPC.desc: Reduce by counting how many participants supplied a true predicate.

DEFER_BLOCKING.desc: Arrive now, block only when the result is actually needed.

LZ.desc: Sample at LOD zero - no mip selection, no derivatives needed.

LL.desc: Sample at an explicitly supplied LOD level.

LB.desc: Sample with an LOD bias added to the computed level.

LOD.desc: Return the computed level of detail instead of sampling.

AOFFI.desc: Apply a constant integer texel offset to the sample coordinates.

DC.desc: Depth compare - the shadow-map sampling path.

NDV.desc: Non-divergent: every lane is known to use the same sampler/texture pair, so the hardware can skip the divergent-sampler loop.

B.desc: Bindless - the texture handle comes from a register instead of a fixed slot.

P.desc: Pipelined sample: the result is delivered later and collected by a separate instruction.

SCR.desc: Scoreboard-tracked variant, for the decoupled/unknown-latency return path.

ARRAY.desc: Array texture - one coordinate selects the slice.

G.desc: Gather the green component from the four selected texels.

mma.desc: Tensor-core matrix multiply-accumulate. The numeric postfix is the MxNxK tile shape.

884.desc: Tile shape M8 N8 K4 - the Volta-generation shape.

16816.desc: Tile shape M16 N8 K16 - the common Ampere FP16 shape.

16832.desc: Tile shape M16 N8 K32 - used by the narrower input types.

STEP0.desc: First of the sub-steps a logical MMA is decomposed into.

STEP1.desc: Second sub-step of the decomposed MMA.

STEP2.desc: Third sub-step of the decomposed MMA.

STEP3.desc: Fourth sub-step of the decomposed MMA.

SP.desc: Structured-sparsity variant: one operand is 2:4 sparse, which doubles throughput.

PASS.desc: Pass the attribute through as interpolated, without applying the perspective divide. The shader does the divide itself, which is why `IPA.PASS` is followed by `MUFU.RCP` of `a[0x7c]` (that slot holds 1/w) and an `FMUL`.

MULTIPLY.desc: Interpolate and multiply by the perspective term in one step.

CONSTANT.desc: Flat / `nointerpolation` attribute - take the provoking vertex's value with no interpolation. Note that a `noperspective` attribute instead shows up as the *absence* of the reciprocal-multiply sequence.

IDX.desc: Dynamically indexed attribute - the slot comes from a register.

CENTROID.desc: Centroid sampling - evaluate inside the covered part of the pixel.

LIVE.desc: Read whether the pixel is still live (not killed and not helper-only).

PHYS.desc: Use the physical attribute address rather than the logical interpolant view.

PACK_AB.desc: Pack the two converted results into one register.

SATFINITE.desc: Saturate out-of-range values to the destination type's finite limits instead of producing an infinity.

NAN.desc: Return NaN when either input is NaN, rather than the non-NaN operand.

XORSIGN.desc: The result's sign is the XOR of the input signs.

64.desc: Read 64 bits into a register pair - what `CS2R.64 Rd, SRZ` uses to clear two registers at once.

-.desc: Negate this source operand. Free - it is an input modifier on the datapath, not a separate instruction.

|x|.desc: Absolute value of this source operand. Free, like negation - the sign bit is simply masked as the operand is read.

!.desc: Logical negation of a predicate operand.

@.desc: Guard predicate. The instruction executes only in the lanes where the predicate holds; the rest are masked off. This is how SASS expresses short divergent regions without branching at all.
